title: Drifting Pebbles vs. Collapsing Spirals: Core Accretion, Pebble Accretion & Gravitational Disk Instability in Planet Formation — Building gas giants before 3-Myr protoplanetary disks vanish; Pollack's three-phase core accretion & Fischer-Valenti's 10^(2[Fe/H]) stellar metallicity triumph; Lambrechts & Johansen's aerodynamic pebble-accretion 1,000x speedup & terrestrial volatile delivery; Boss's Toomre-Q gravitational disk instability, ALMA's <1-Myr HL Tau rings, Currie's 93-AU embedded protoplanet AB Aur b & Stefansson's K2-25b M-dwarf dust-budget crisis; Hill pebble vs. Toomre-Q math, JWST C/O + refractory power & spotting planet-formation tests in disguise

teenKit.tldr: Baby planets must build massive gas-giant bodies out of cosmic dust before stellar winds blow away their nurseries in just 2 to 3 million years. To beat this ticking clock, young worlds rely on either slow core accretion supercharged by sweeping up millimeter-sized pebbles or instant gravitational disk collapse.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how planets win the race against disappearing cosmic gas reveals the violent, chaotic origins of our own home and explains why worlds like Earth and Jupiter exist at all.
keyTakeaways: Protoplanetary disks act as giant cosmic construction sites made of 99% gas and 1% dust, but starlight acts like a blowtorch, evaporating these nurseries within a few million years.

Core accretion traditionally builds planets by gathering rocks slowly, but the pebble-accretion revolution speeds this up a thousandfold by letting seeds sweep up drifting debris like sticky vacuum cleaners.
Gravitational disk instability offers an alternative fast lane where cold, massive outer disks instantly snap and fragment into giant planets in just thousands of years.

vocab.meaning: A flat, spinning cloud of gas and dust surrounding a newborn star where planets are born.
The slow, step-by-step process of building a planet by gathering solid rocks until it gets heavy enough to suck up surrounding gas.
An aerodynamic shortcut where a growing planetary core catches passing pebbles that slow down due to gas drag and fall right into its gravity well.
A top-down process where a massive outer disk suddenly collapses under its own weight, breaking apart into giant planets in a blink of an eye.

quiz.question: What is the main cosmic threat that giant planets must race against while forming?
options: Stellar winds evaporating the gas disk within a few million years
Collisions with rogue black holes passing through the galaxy
Running out of heavy metals like iron in the universe
Freezing temperatures turning all hydrogen into solid ice
quiz.explanation: Newborn stars blast intense radiation that strips away their surrounding planet-forming gas disks in just 2 to 5 million years.

quiz.question: How does pebble accretion solve the problem of the speedy disk deadline?
options: It uses magnetic fields to teleport rocks directly into planetary cores.
It uses aerodynamic drag to help growing seeds scoop up drifting pebbles a thousand times faster.
It completely bypasses the need for solid cores by turning gas directly into rock.
It stops stellar winds from blowing away the disk altogether.
quiz.explanation: As gas slows down pebbles through friction, they lose momentum and get trapped by the growing planet's gravity, speeding up growth massively.

quiz.question: What is gravitational disk instability?
options: When a star spins so fast it tears its own planets apart
A slow, methodical accumulation of space dust over billions of years
A top-down process where cold outer disks fracture and collapse directly into giant planets
The sudden melting of ice giants due to nearby supernova explosions
quiz.explanation: Instead of building up from tiny dust specks, heavy outer disks can snap and fragment under their own gravity to form planets in thousands of years.
